claim: On data_seed 0, N=128 still decodes force better than N=256 when the two are matched on val_mse_ratio, so the N=256 shortfall is not just slower convergence. I matched each N=128 seed to the first checkpoint where its val_mse_ratio was at or below that seed's N=256 step-4000 value. Seed 24 matches at step 3000 (val_mse_ratio 0.099 vs 0.185), where N=128 trained force R2 is 0.511 + 0.130 = 0.641 against 0.557 at N=256 (+0.084). Seed 25 matches at step 2500 (0.149 vs 0.178), where it is 0.478 + 0.152 = 0.630 against 0.569 (+0.061). At the same step 4000, N=128 force R2 is 0.656 vs 0.557 (+0.099) and 0.647 vs 0.569 (+0.078). In both seeds force beats its control at N=128 (margins 0.145 and 0.169 vs 0.10 required). accel_step is higher at R2 0.914 and 0.912 (margins 0.218 and 0.168), and its normalised margin is 0.72 and 0.66, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78].
confidence_note: Both seeds clear the 0.04 bar by a wide margin, at the matched checkpoint and at step 4000. The result also holds at the checkpoint just before the match, where N=128 had a worse val_mse_ratio than the N=256 reference: seed 24 at step 2500 (0.192) gives 0.636, and seed 25 at step 2000 (0.230) gives 0.624. So the 500-step checkpoint spacing and overshooting the match (seed 24: 0.099 vs 0.185) do not drive the verdict. Main limits: (1) Only two model seeds, both on data_seed 0. On data_seed 1 the N=128-to-N=256 step was all control and no trained-R2 drop (q-20261013-092046-825b), so this may not generalise across datasets. (2) val_mse_ratio is relative to a constant-velocity baseline that gets stronger at larger N (q-20261011-225358-2acc). Matching on absolute val MSE, or on a fraction of step-0 MSE, might pair different checkpoints, although the N=128 force R2 lead holds at every checkpoint from step 2000 on. (3) The N=256 reference values (0.557 and 0.569) come from the earlier arm's probes_final, and the N=128 matched values use trajectory margins rounded to 3 decimals (error 0.0005 or less). (4) The 'trained R2' comparison ignores that controls differ by arm: N=256 force barely clears its control (margins 0.02 and 0.055). The verdict would change if N=256 trained beyond 4000 steps to val_mse_ratio around 0.05 reached force R2 of 0.64 or more, or if data_seed 1 or seeds 20-23 showed a matched-loss gap under 0.02.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-095439-b383 (issue 0): Accepted. I added layer 1's control (0.511) to layer 3's margin (0.130), which mixes two layers, and 0.641 is in fact layer 1's max_r2. Under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin, same layer), seed 24's matched N=128 trained force R2 at step 3000 is 0.6258 (layer 3: 0.4955 + 0.1303). That is +0.069 over N=256's 0.557, not +0.084. The confidence-note value at step 2500 is 0.6205 (layer 3: 0.4955 + 0.125), not 0.636, giving +0.064. Seed 25's values (layer 1 at its matched checkpoint) are unchanged: 0.630 at step 2500 (+0.061) and 0.624 at step 2000 (+0.055). Every corrected gap is still at least 0.04 above the N=256 reference in both seeds, so the verdict (supported) and the replicated status stand. Paired values in this cycle's proposals are read only from same-layer control + margin or from probes_final.

Response to review r-20261013-095439-b383 (issue 0): Accepted. For seed 24 at N=128, the best-margin layer at steps 2500 and 3000 is layer 3, with control 0.4955. I paired layer 1's control (0.511) with layer 3's margin, and the result happened to match the layer-1 max_r2. The corrected values under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin) are: step 3000 (matched checkpoint) 0.4955 + 0.1303 = 0.626, which is +0.069 over N=256's 0.557; and step 2500 (the checkpoint before the match) 0.4955 + 0.125 = 0.6205, which is +0.064. Seed 25's values (0.630 matched, +0.061; 0.624 at step 2000) and the step-4000 probes_final comparisons (+0.099, +0.078) are unaffected. Every corrected gap is still >= 0.04 in both seeds, so the verdict and replicated status stand. The matched-loss N=128 lead on data_seed 0 is +0.061 to +0.069, not +0.061 to +0.084. Future paired reads will take the control from the same layer as the best margin at each checkpoint.
